qaLog.a: AI writes both example tables and tests; humans review. Patterns repeat across CT, so derive the principle once. Tests also needed for services, not only answer checking.

decisions.decision: Spec-driven: spec -> example tables -> tests -> code -> review; AI writes tables and tests and raises ambiguous cases as questions; separate sessions for tests and code; frozen tests (D30)

Layers: vision, architecture, contracts, module specs, decisions, agent briefs. One file per domain module in catalog/, platform/, personalization/; header names owner and implementing services; each rule has one home and an ID
Both write all parts; teammate leads Go backend and reviews Go tests; user leads product idea, architecture, infra and reviews example tables. Owner field = approver, not sole author
Go core; Python for catalog CI and composer (symbolic checking dropped by D80). Supersedes D34

Knowledge model and optimizer run in a Python worker fed by the PostgreSQL queue; Go core owns all student transactions (attempts, lesson marks, edits); Python owns derived tables (p, forecast, plan). Worker down = stale plan, no data loss (D35)

Go core picks the next diagnostic item by a deterministic rule over the prerequisite graph and current test answers (D7); no Python call during the test; on completion the worker seeds the knowledge model

AI agent runs in the Python worker and shares one LLM adapter with the composer (D36); Go validates every proposal on save (schema, allowed_actions, rights, plan version D24); approved proposals reach the optimizer as constraints

Only CT answer formats, checked synchronously in Go. Ambiguity is removed at the source: every template must yield an unambiguous answer (integer, or the statement says how to scale it), enforced by CI task_rules (D27). Symbolic checking is not planned

Model and plan are recalculated only on: homework submitted with the explicit 'submit' button, lesson marked by tutor, diagnostics finished. No per-answer recalculation. Unsubmitted homework is not treated as failed: plan stays as is until submission, then adapts (one lesson later). Raw attempts are visible to the tutor before submission
Tutor records two marks per lesson: last theory block explained and last practice task solved

Phase 1 (now): CT catalog is built with a Claude skill run by the tutor in chat; used with real students; the tutor-approved catalog becomes the gold standard. Phase 2 (coursework): composer as an explicit LangGraph graph (pipeline) vs the skill (agent), both measured against the gold. Evaluation is a separate module (catalog/eval) running the composer in isolation with no access to the catalog; details deferred

While generating lesson materials and catalog changes, the tutor's remarks to the agent (what was produced, what was changed, why) are recorded as structured notes next to the change; this corpus later shapes the composer graph or skill and its evaluation. Storage format to be fixed in the catalog spec

Release 1: block library (D43) + lesson assembly + mobile site + PDF + homework from ready variants with Go autocheck, 'submit', tutor sees results; catalog limited to near-term topics but in final catalog format with permanent ids. Release 2: catalog frequencies + rough plan for the goal. Release 3: knowledge model worker. Release 4: agent. First spec: catalog schema, then answer check, attempts log. Tracks run in parallel: catalog via skill (user), platform skeleton (teammate)

Telegram Login on the site: tutor creates the student and sends a one-time expiring invite link; first login binds Telegram; session in an httpOnly cookie for 90 days, revocable by the tutor; bot links open the site directly. No passwords. Server verifies the Telegram login hash (HMAC with the bot token) and auth_date freshness; Telegram id is personal data stored with PII (D17). Mini App and other methods later

docs/spec/glossary.md defines every domain term once; all module specs share one template (purpose, IO via contract, numbered rules, example tables, errors, out of scope); one file per module, folder only past ~300 lines

Two classes of triggers. New facts (homework submitted, checkpoint test, mock exam, diagnostics finished, lesson marked, recheck after key correction, imported RT results) -> recalculate knowledge model and plan. New constraints (tutor edit, approved agent proposal, goal, exam date, hours budget, new catalog version) -> recalculate plan only. Nothing per single answer

RIKZ sends the answer sheet and the variant. (1) Variant markup is shared catalog work, once per RT variant: tasks mapped to types and difficulty by the two-AI markup with tutor resolving disagreements. (2) Student answers enter the attempt log with source=RT and mock-level weight (D45); our checker computes correct/incorrect against the key, wrong answers are matched to traps (D11). Entry: tutor form for 30 answers first; later AI pre-fills from the PDF and the tutor confirms. Not in release 1

At most one recalculation per student at a time (per-student lock). Each job records the id of the last journal event it read; derived results (p, forecast, plan) are written only if no newer event for that student exists, otherwise the job restarts from fresh state (fast-forward-only semantics). Covered by a concurrency test

Per branch of the prerequisite graph, the boundary of knowledge is located by binary search: start mid-branch; success moves up, failure moves down. Trust rule (matches D46): one correct part-B answer, or two correct part-A answers on different tasks, counts the level and the prerequisites below it as known. Two failures at a level mark everything above it as not mastered without asking. An abandoned test seeds the model with what was solved, the rest stays 'not checked'; the test can be resumed. The rule is one example table shared by the Go diagnostics and the Python model. Branches are DAG paths: how the middle is chosen is fixed in the diagnostics spec

One Python worker codebase, two running instances with separate queues: recalc (knowledge model, optimizer, plan) and agent (LLM calls with a hard timeout). Plain synchronous code, no asyncio. Tutor cabinet shows 'plan as of <time>' for every student; if recalc lags a submitted event by more than N minutes, the tutor gets a Telegram alert

One PostgreSQL, schema per owner: core.* written only by Go (journal, lesson marks, edits, students, PII), compute.* written only by the Python worker (p, forecast, plan). Single-writer rule per table. Worker DB role reads the journal and catalog through views without PII and has no access to PII tables. Queue jobs are claimed with FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED. Agent proposals reach Go through an internal API that validates and answers accepted/rejected with a reason. A CI test asserts the role grants. Pattern: CQRS (facts in core, derived views in compute)

decisions.topic: Consent and account protection (amends D86, RT6)
decisions.decision: Parental consent: before the student invite, the tutor sends the parent a link with a short 'what we store and why' text and an 'I agree' button; the system records date, text version and method; the student invite does not work without consent; consent can be revoked via the same link. Invite binding: the tutor is notified in Telegram which account was bound and can unbind and reissue in one action. Tutor account: 7-day session, every login from a new device is confirmed in Telegram and reported

decisions.topic: Bot links and login transport (amends D86, RT7)
decisions.decision: Telegram login stays for release 1. Bot links carry no secrets and are safe to forward. With a valid cookie the link opens the page directly; without one (e.g. Telegram in-app browser cleared it) the page offers one-tap 'Log in with Telegram'. Login data travels only in the request body, never in the URL, and never reaches logs. Documented procedure to rotate the bot token (invalidates login signatures; sessions survive). Password login and Mini App are later options

Release 2 = catalog frequencies + rough plan + adaptive diagnostics (D90). Student state for the plan before the knowledge model exists = diagnostics result plus tutor overrides per type ('base mastered' / 'automatism', D71); tutor overrides win. From release 3 the knowledge model keeps this state current. Diagnostic types catalog package is prepared for release 2 (moves D41's 'before release 1')

decisions.topic: Carry-over with two lesson marks (amends D9/D82, RT9)
decisions.decision: Every practice task is linked to the theory block it depends on. After the two marks: unsolved tasks whose theory was explained -> homework (plus D39 reinforcement); tasks whose theory was not explained move with that theory to the start of the next lesson. Homework is assembled and issued only after the tutor's marks

decisions.topic: Single source of contracts (supersedes S3/D57 'TS schemas', RT10)
decisions.decision: docs/contracts holds OpenAPI (HTTP APIs, incl. the internal proposals API) and JSON Schema (queue events, catalog format). Go, Python and TS types are generated from them; hand-written duplicates are forbidden. All DB migrations (core and compute schemas) live in one place with one ordering. CI on every PR checks that generated code matches the contracts and runs contract tests

decisions.topic: Phase-1 catalog path and notes privacy (RT11)
decisions.decision: Catalog produced by the skill follows the normal path: PR -> CI -> key checks (D56) -> tutor merge; no shortcut into the database. Tutor notes (D84) refer to students by pseudonym and pass a PII filter before storage. Gold-standard independence for the composer comparison stays open for the catalog/eval spec (user deferred it)

User reviews Python tests (knowledge model, optimizer); teammate reviews Go tests; the module owner from the spec header merges. Expected values in reference tests never come from the code under test: hand-computed small examples or an independent second solver

decisions.topic: Release-1 lesson and homework assembly (R3 Q-A1)
decisions.decision: Release-1 plan = import of the existing static plan from ct-2027 (PLAN.md + plan/L*.md frontmatter: lesson, week, phase, kind, topics, review). Before each lesson the composer skill converts the L-file into library blocks and the lesson composition (PR -> tutor review); the library grows lesson by lesson. Homework is assembled by the system after the two lesson marks (D96 + D39), reviewed and issued by the tutor. Lesson marks and carry-over are in release 1. From release 2 the optimizer adapts this static plan; the static plan doubles as the expert reference to compare the optimizer against

Release 1 uses ready variants only: the skill prepares 5-10 variants per type for each lesson; independent key check in CI is mandatory and blocks the PR on mismatch. The catalog schema already models templates; template expansion arrives in release 2. When a student has no unseen variant of a type left, the tutor gets a 'variants needed' warning and the type is left out of the homework (no repeats, D27)

Release-1 Telegram messages: to the tutor - account bound to a student, login from a new device (D93), student submitted homework (score + link); to the student - new homework issued (link). No reminders in release 1. Sent from Go through an outbox table with retry; a failed send never blocks the triggering action

decisions.topic: Partial credit and input normalisation (R3 Q-B1)
decisions.decision: Scoring for B1, B2 and multi-answer A6/A10 follows the official RIKZ rules (2026 spec, then 2027). An agent transcribes them into an example table with a reference to the spec clause; the tutor verifies it. Rules live in the CT subject package as data, not in Go code; the same package holds input normalisation (spaces, separators, digit order, empty answer)

decisions.topic: Attempt lifecycle by assignment kind (R3 Q-C1, Q-C2; refines D11/D12)
decisions.decision: Homework: every answer is sent and checked at once and becomes an immutable attempt; part B: after a wrong first attempt only 'wrong' is shown, answer and solution after the second; part A: one attempt. Submit is allowed with unanswered tasks after a confirmation ('N left'), is final, shows the summary (per-task result, solutions to failed tasks, a 'did not understand' button that adds the task to the 'discuss at lesson' list) and notifies the tutor. Tests (checkpoint, mock, diagnostics): one attempt per task, results shown to the student only at the end; diagnostics checks each answer internally to choose the next item (D90) without showing it

Per student and subject the tutor sets a schedule rule (weekdays, time, duration in minutes). The system expands it into dated lessons up to the exam date; single lessons can be moved, cancelled or added. For the current student the schedule is taken from the imported ct-2027 PLAN.md

A cancelled lesson moves as a whole to the next date and every later lesson shifts by one; no homework is issued; the cancellation is recorded as its own event (distinct from 'nothing covered'). If the plan no longer fits before the exam, the tutor is warned and can add a make-up lesson (D105); from release 2 the optimizer compresses the plan instead

Homework size is set per student: each task has a minutes estimate and homework fits the student's own homework time budget between lessons (D42). Fill order: unsolved tasks -> D39 reinforcement -> new tasks; what did not fit is shown to the tutor in the review. Default deadline is the start of the next lesson in that subject, adjustable per student. Interpretation of a truncated answer ('под каждого ученика индивидуально, в...'), open to correction

Release 1 has two roles: student and tutor. Every student has exactly one owning tutor; a tutor sees and acts only on own students (checked in Go on every request). The owner field exists in the schema from day one; admin role and transferring a student are later. The parent is not a role: only the giver of consent (D93). The first tutor account is created by a server CLI command

decisions.topic: Student leaving and consent revocation (R3 Q-M2; makes D18 concrete)
decisions.decision: Leaving = archive: login blocked, all sessions revoked, data kept, reversible by the tutor. Consent revocation = anonymisation: the PII row and Telegram id are deleted at once, sessions revoked; attempts stay under a random pseudonym no longer linked to anyone; tutor notes go through the same pseudonym rule (D98). PII disappears from backups when the backup copies expire (retention set in the backup spec)

Consent is the 'I agree' button on the link the tutor sends to the parent (D93); the parent's identity is not verified, the tutor is responsible for sending the link to the parent. Accepted risk: a student pressing the button via a forwarded link cannot be detected. Kept: consent is asked again on a new text version; at 18 the student consents personally. Upgrade path (parent Telegram login) stays possible without redesign. Interviewer recommended parent Telegram login; user chose the simpler button

decisions.topic: Database hosting and backups (R3 Q-N1; supersedes S4 'managed PostgreSQL' and 'one backend service')
decisions.decision: PostgreSQL runs as a container in Docker Compose on the project server. WAL archive and a daily encrypted full copy go to S3-compatible storage at a different provider (e.g. pgBackRest), giving point-in-time recovery (S6). A nightly restore drill runs in a throwaway container and recalculates derived data from the journal. The backup encryption key is also kept outside the server (user's password manager). Service layout follows D33/D91, not S4

decisions.topic: Core glossary terms (R3 Q-F1; seeds glossary.md, D77)
decisions.decision: блок = library piece (theory, rule, worked example, typical error, widget); этап урока = timed part of a lesson; серия = consecutive tasks of one type; вариант = concrete task instance with numbers and a permanent id; тест (сессия) = a whole CT/CE/RT paper; опция = an answer option in part A; элемент = knowledge element within a topic (D70); пункт спецификации = RIKZ spec item; тип задания = what is checked (D3); позиция = place in the test (A1..B20); задача = UI word only, docs say вариант. Earlier decisions are read through this table

decisions.topic: Coursework experiment design (R3 Q-P1; amends D83 phase 2)
decisions.decision: Phase 2 compares two approaches on the same models: agent = free tool-calling loop over the composer's tools; pipeline = explicit LangGraph graph. Both use the shared LLM adapter and run on local models (Ollama) and on Claude; the phase-1 Claude skill is only an upper reference. Two tasks: (1) build a curriculum catalog from sources, (2) check a curriculum with deliberately seeded errors (missing topic, wrong prerequisite order, uncited element) and report them - this matches the topic 'checking study programs'. Phase 2 starts after release 1; milestone spring 2027
Permanent id on every level (topic, element, type, subvariant, variant, block); ids are never reused
Typo/formatting keeps the id; changed numbers or statement = new variant, old one retired from issue but kept for history; fixing a wrong key keeps the id and triggers recheck (D22)
Transfer map states explicitly which old ids map to which new ids; past attempts follow the map

decisions.topic: Open homework vs new catalog version (R3 default 01#1)
decisions.decision: Issued but unsubmitted homework stays on the catalog version it was issued with; key fixes reach it through recheck
Separate catalog.* schema; its only writer is the CI loader
Any key-check mismatch blocks the PR until the tutor resolves it
Publishing a lesson stores an immutable snapshot: block ids, order, catalog_version
Every answer and Submit request carries an idempotency key; a retry returns the original result without a new attempt
Unique key student+sitting+test; re-import is an idempotent upsert
Key correction triggers recheck through an internal Go API with correction_id and batch state; resumes after failure
catalog_version is part of the recalc job input and the stored plan; a plan from an older version cannot overwrite a newer one
Jobs are claimed with a lease and attempt counter; on worker crash the lease expires and another instance takes it; after N failures status=failed and alert
Release 1 runs without the Python worker: Go writes the journal; queue and compute.* arrive in release 2; key recheck runs synchronously in Go in release 1
A one-shot migrate step runs before services start; migrations are expand-only; rollback = previous image tags
prod and staging on one server on subdomains, staging has its own test bot; local dev uses a test login without Telegram
A service Telegram chat for the user: service down, disk > 80%, backup or restore drill failed, LLM budget exhausted; recalc lag alert to the tutor
Secrets live in a file on the server outside git (mode 600, Compose secrets), with a copy in the user's password manager; rotation checklist per secret
Frozen test paths are listed in CODEOWNERS; CI blocks a code PR that changes them; a wrong test is fixed in a separate PR approved by the module owner
AI raises an ambiguity as 'Open question Q-n' in the module spec; it blocks tests for that rule; the owner's answer becomes an example-table row with the rule id
Example tables are YAML next to the spec; Go and Python tests are generated from them
Integration tests (incl. D89 concurrency) run against a real PostgreSQL container, synthetic pseudonymous data only
Block text is Markdown + LaTeX (KaTeX); widget = {widget, params} per JSON Schema; figures SVG; PDF rendered on the server, every widget has a static print version
One input component per CT answer format; malformed input is rejected client-side and does not count as an attempt
Attempt has two fields: source (homework, lesson, checkpoint, mock, diagnostics, RT) sets weight; place (home/lesson) is stored only
The tutor resolves a dispute either by fixing the key for everyone or by a 'manual verdict' event for one attempt; verdicts are always derived from the journal
Pseudonym = permanent random short code; PII = name, Telegram id, parent contact, school; the notes filter replaces known names and blocks phone numbers and @usernames

decisions.topic: Release-1 content cadence and fallback (R4-Q1; amends D100)
decisions.decision: The skill prepares lessons in batches 2-4 weeks ahead in one PR, not one PR per lesson. If a lesson's blocks are not ready, the site shows the lesson from its L-file as is (PDF/HTML) and the tutor picks homework from already loaded variants; automatic homework assembly applies whenever blocks and variants exist. A lesson is never blocked by the content pipeline

Catalog and scoring rules are tagged with the spec version they follow ('RIKZ 2026') and work proceeds now. When the 2027 spec is published, one reconciliation PR records what changed, what is retired and what is added, using the transfer map (D116) and versioned scoring rules (D103); students are not blocked

decisions.topic: Public code repo vs private catalog (R4-Q3; replaces S8 premise)
decisions.decision: knowgap-lab/ai-mentor (public) holds code, specs and a small synthetic demo catalog only. The real catalog with answer keys and the tutor notes (D84) live in a separate private repository. No student details (name, city, goal, scores, class) are ever committed to the public repo. Pre-push rule: the local docs/platform-spec branch is squashed before its first push so commits that contained such details never reach GitHub

decisions.topic: Server loss: RTO and rebuild drill (R4-Q4; extends D111)
decisions.decision: Single server stays. Target RTO <= 24 h after total server loss: the whole stack is rebuilt on a clean machine by a script from git plus the off-site backup. Once a quarter the user performs a real rebuild on a new machine and records the time. During an outage homework continues via PDF

decisions.topic: Review ownership (R4-Q5; refines D74, D99, D131)
decisions.decision: The user (tutor) must approve only subject matter: catalog content and keys, scoring and normalisation rules and subject example tables, consent text. Engineering PRs (code, infra, technical tests, contracts) are merged by the teammate on green CI without the tutor. Encoded in CODEOWNERS

decisions.topic: Safe consent revocation (R4-Q6; amends D93, D109)
decisions.decision: Opening a consent link never changes state; giving or revoking consent requires pressing a button (POST), so link-preview bots cannot trigger it. On revocation the student's login is blocked and sessions revoked immediately and the tutor is notified; PII deletion/anonymisation runs after 7 days, during which a mistaken revocation can be undone. Link tokens are stored hashed, never logged, rate-limited per IP

decisions.topic: Homework recipe (R4-Q7; replaces the D107 fill rule, confirms the D107 budget meaning)
decisions.decision: Homework follows the lesson's recipe from its L-file, turned into data by the skill together with the lesson blocks: A = new topic series by rising difficulty; B = interleaved review of the plan's review topics; C = CT-format mixed tasks with a timer (autochecked, results at the end like a test); D = flashcards and E = re-read/checklist (shown as a checklist, not checked). Distributed by days (Mon-Fri, Saturday as reserve). Unsolved tasks from the lesson and D39 reinforcement go first into block A. Budget = the student's weekly homework time (currently about 6 h); per-variant minutes come from the skill. Deadline = next lesson in the subject

DEFERRED: focus is the MVP for real students. Open items recorded for later: phase-2 timeline (parallel on a catalog snapshot vs after release 1), hardware for local models (a paid server is acceptable), seeded-error dataset (>= 40 samples, no real student data), README rewrite to match D113, agreeing the topic interpretation with the supervisor. Revisit after release 1 is defined in specs

decisions.topic: Operational numbers (R4-Q9; makes D8, D86, D91, D93, D101, D111, D125 testable)
decisions.decision: Invite link: 72 h, single use (expired/used -> 410, no session). Telegram login rejected if now - auth_date > 300 s or HMAC mismatch (401). Tutor new-device: unknown device_id cookie -> pending session, confirm in Telegram within 10 min else rejected. Variants: CI blocks a lesson PR if a used type has < 5 active variants (pool_too_small); skill default 8. Recalc lag alert: oldest unprocessed event older than 15 min -> one alert per student until recovered. Queue: lease 120 s, backoff 30 s x 2^(attempt-1), failed after 5 attempts + ops alert. Plan horizon: lessons 1-2 frozen, lessons up to +42 days planned by blocks, beyond = weekly milestones only. Backup retention: 30 days. All are configuration values
A task type has one primary knowledge element; other elements are prerequisites. Subvariant is its own entity with a permanent id. The checkpoint reserve is a flag on the variant
B3-B20: exact integer, no rounding; scaling only via a phrase from a fixed list; B1: bijection; B2: digits ascending without repeats; violations fail CI
5 distinct options; no distractor equals the key; number of correct options explicit (A6/A10); every distractor carries a trap id
Every lesson stage has a minutes estimate; capacity = duration minus error review; after carry-over the overflow from the end moves to the first unfrozen lesson
A checkpoint is a lesson stage; its contents are fixed when the lesson freezes
Fixed expiry from login; unbind and invite reissue revoke all student sessions; tutor access recovery via a server CLI command
Briefs are assembled by a script from the module spec header (rules, tables, contracts, glossary, allowed paths); test paths are write-protected for code sessions
Thin job {student_id, model|plan, trigger_event_id}; pending jobs of one student merge (model absorbs plan); watermark = single core journal sequence covering facts and constraints
Go reads v_plan_current and v_forecast described by JSON Schema; plan is an immutable snapshot with plan_version, based_on_event_id, computed_at; Go role has SELECT only
POST /internal/proposals with idempotency_key, based_on_plan_version; stale -> rejected stale_plan, agent regenerates once; approval writes a constraint event; service token
Release-1 build order: catalog contract -> loader -> variant page -> Go check -> journal -> tutor screen (local dev login); then Telegram login and consent; then conspect and PDF
Citation required for every element/topic/type, task_rules and element-level prerequisites; the skill uses temporary keys, CI mints permanent ids at merge; profile sits next to the catalog
diagnostic_abandoned and diagnostic_resumed are journal events with a session version; abandonment triggers seeding
After a recalc commit the worker enqueues AgentTrigger carrying journal and plan revisions

Lesson template in the catalog; per-student lesson composition, calendar and homework in core.* written by Go; the optimizer writes only compute.plan and Go applies it to unfrozen lessons; the imported static plan lives in core.* as version 0 and expert reference
Issue, approve, withdraw and submit of an assignment are immutable core events with a full snapshot of variants and rules; lesson snapshot includes practice variants and stages
Attempts reference the internal student id; the pseudonym and its link live next to PII and are deleted with it
__Host- cookies, SameSite=Lax, CSRF token and Origin check on all POSTs, new session id at login and binding; staging on a separate registrable domain
CI rejects raw HTML and dangerous SVG elements; KaTeX trust:false; sanitiser at render; strict CSP without inline scripts
Messages and logs reference only the pseudonym; a revocation log is re-applied after any restore
Single authorization layer in Go over (role, tutor_id, student_id) for every object; idempotency keys bound to the user; permission table generates tests
Per-service and per-environment tokens with narrow method sets; separate Docker networks for prod and staging; external texts in prompts marked as data
AI pre-fill of RT sheets runs only on a local model and name fields are cut out before the call
Queue lives in its own schema queue.*: insertion via a function by Go and worker; lease and status changed only by the worker; grants checked in CI
The loader calls a Go internal API; Go writes one global event and per-student jobs keyed student+catalog_version
Outbox key = type + event id + recipient; Telegram id read at send time; pending messages cancelled on archive or anonymisation
Manual verdict and tutor type override = facts; lesson cancellation and schedule change = constraints; archiving cancels the student's queued jobs
One event per student and correction_id; one message to the tutor listing changed homework; the student is not messaged
A periodic Go check emits alerts through the outbox; warnings are a cabinet banner plus Telegram to the tutor
On first start the worker replays each student's journal from zero; until then Go shows the imported plan marked 'not recalculated'; lag alerts only for events after launch
Until the knowledge model (release 3), a simple rule applies: a failed type gets a review in the plan
Go writes a versioned canonical observation event per attempt; Python only consumes it; replay vectors test both
A small hand-confirmed acceptance suite from official rules and real tutor cases can overrule AI-written tables
An attempt references its assignment or RT import; source is derived from the assignment kind
A test (CT/CE/RT paper) is a catalog entity with 1:N appearances; the sitting date is stored in core
Exam date and hours budget are set per student+subject; a shared budget is their sum with a minimum share
D80 applies to the CT package only; answer checking is a subject-package interface

decisions.topic: Agent actions (R4 01#7; resolves D5 vs D50)
decisions.decision: Agent actions per P8/D50: swap_hw_tasks and marking error causes; repetitions and ordering are planner-only; insert_review and reorder removed

decisions.topic: Frequency window (R4 01#8; resolves D1 vs D61)
decisions.decision: Frequencies from CT and CE 2023-2026, window rolls yearly; RT is marked up but not counted; older appearances = 'seen'
At least 2 variants per subvariant for each lesson topic so D39 is always possible; CI blocks the PR otherwise
Telegram login widget requests write access; undelivered messages are flagged in the cabinet, homework link stays there
Static plan import is one-time from L-file frontmatter; topic codes (M01...) map to catalog ids via a table in the catalog package
CI builds a signed catalog artifact; a one-shot loader container on the server applies it to staging, then to prod on command
Lessons of kind diagnostic or test from the static plan are normal lessons in release 1; forms are printed as PDF, answers not entered
The skill flattens conditional steps into a linear order; each practice variant links to its theory block; variants used in class count as seen, no attempts recorded
Birth date stored as PII; consent text versioned in the repo; the tutor copies the parent link from the cabinet; the current student also goes through consent
Before issue the tutor can remove/add a variant from the pool, change the deadline, issue; after issue only withdraw as a whole before the first answer
From release 2 the optimizer starts from the static plan; frozen, published lessons and manual shifts are constraints; it deviates only when the gain exceeds hysteresis
An immutable import snapshot (file hashes) is kept; a divergence report for the tutor is monitoring, not a test oracle
Covered topics are seeded by tutor marks; diagnostics runs only on uncovered branches with unseen variants
Ready variants get a subvariant at load; CI drops generated duplicates; pool and reserve counted per type
